title: Tensor compatibility of the etale/pro-etale open-extension comparison
statement:
Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion] and $A$ a finite discrete commutative ring. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module-sheaf categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], comparison inverse images $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and $e=j_!^{et}$, $d=j_!^{pro}$, $r=j_{et}^{-1}$, $s=j_{pro}^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Let $a:C_Ur\xrightarrow{\sim}sC_X$ be the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and let $c:C_Xe\xrightarrow{\sim}dC_U$ be the unit-normalized canonical open comparison [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization]. All tensors below are ordinary sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Write $t^T_{V,W}:C_T(V\otimes_A W)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_TV\otimes_A C_TW$ for the canonical tensor comparison, induced by inverse image and the constant-ring identification.

For $F\in\operatorname{Mod}(U_{et},A)$ and $B\in\operatorname{Mod}(X_{et},A)$, let $\kappa^e_{F,B}:e(F\otimes_A rB)\to eF\otimes_A B$ be the $e\dashv r$ transpose of $\eta^e_F\otimes1$ under the restriction-tensor comparison, and define $\kappa^d_{G,H}:d(G\otimes_A sH)\to dG\otimes_A H$ by the same open-unit prescription on the pro-etale site. Then
$$
(c_F\otimes1)\circ t^X_{eF,B}\circ C_X(\kappa^e_{F,B})
=\kappa^d_{C_UF,C_XB}\circ d\bigl((1\otimes a_B)\circ t^U_{F,rB}\bigr)\circ c_{F\otimes_A rB}.
$$
Both sides have source $C_Xe(F\otimes_A rB)$ and target $dC_UF\otimes_A C_XB$. The equality is natural in both $F$ and $B$.

source.place: Tag 09AF, label lemma-jshriek-comparison, proof by the common right adjoint; agent refinement recording tensor compatibility of the etale/pro-etale open-extension comparison

proof.text:
Write $N=F\otimes_A rB$ and $M=dC_UF\otimes_A C_XB$. The etale open adjunction is [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. On the pro-etale site, [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies the open with the localized site and its constant ring, so [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] gives $d\dashv s$. For any $h:C_XeN\to M$ put
$$\Psi(h)=s(h)\circ a_{eN}\circ C_U(\eta^e_N):C_UN\to sM.$$
The unit equation of [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization] gives
$$\Psi(h)=s(h\circ c_N^{-1})\circ\eta^d_{C_UN}.$$
Thus $\Psi$ is injective: precomposition with the isomorphism $c_N^{-1}$ is a bijection and the subsequent formula is the Hom bijection of $d\dashv s$. In particular equality of the two proposed maps can be checked by this formula; no faithfulness of $s$ on all sheaves is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison: common-right-adjoint argument; module open adjunction: sites-modules.tex Tag 03DI, lemma-extension-by-zero

proof.text:
Let $\rho^e_{V,W}:r(V\otimes_AW)\xrightarrow{\sim}rV\otimes_A rW$ and $\rho^d_{H,J}:s(H\otimes_AJ)\xrightarrow{\sim}sH\otimes_A sJ$ be the restriction-tensor maps. These and $t^T$ are the canonical module pullback comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. The constant-ring identification [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact](1) identifies $C_T$ with its algebraic inverse image. Applied to these inverse images, [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison] fixes their values on transported pure tensors. For the canonical comparison $a$ of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] this gives
$$\rho^d_{C_XV,C_XW}\circ s(t^X_{V,W})\circ a_{V\otimes_AW}
=(a_V\otimes a_W)\circ t^U_{rV,rW}\circ C_U(\rho^e_{V,W}).\tag{*}$$
Here is the elementary verification, to avoid assuming a tensor-coherence clause in the pullback-comparison node. On underlying set sheaves, naturality of $a$ with the two product projections says $a_{V\times W}=a_V\times a_W$ through the finite-product identifications. Naturality with the universal pure pairing $V\times W\to V\otimes_AW$ then says that both sides of (*) send a transported pure pair $(x,y)$ to $a_V(x)\otimes a_W(y)$. The scalar maps agree on the constant ring $A$, so this is an equality of balanced pairings. Pure pairings determine linear tensor maps by [def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus]. This proves (*) without a sectionwise description of arbitrary sections of a sheafified tensor.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, and Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product: universal bilinear pairing; comparison is the canonical underlying inverse-image isomorphism

proof.text:
Denote the left-hand side in the statement by $L$. By the definition of $\kappa^e$ as the transpose of the unit tensored with the identity,
$$\rho^e_{eF,B}\circ r(\kappa^e_{F,B})\circ\eta^e_N=\eta^e_F\otimes1_{rB}.$$
Naturality of $a$ with $\kappa^e$ gives
$$\Psi(L)=s(c_F\otimes1)\circ s(t^X_{eF,B})\circ a_{eF\otimes_AB}\circ C_U\bigl(r(\kappa^e_{F,B})\circ\eta^e_N\bigr).$$
Apply (*) of step 2 to $(eF,B)$, and use naturality of $\rho^d$ with $c_F\otimes1$ and of $t^U$ with $\eta^e_F\otimes1$. The displayed defining equation for $\kappa^e$ reduces this to
$$\rho^d_{dC_UF,C_XB}\circ\Psi(L)
=\bigl((s(c_F)\circ a_{eF}\circ C_U(\eta^e_F))\otimes a_B\bigr)\circ t^U_{F,rB}.$$
The parenthesized first factor is exactly $\eta^d_{C_UF}$ by [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization]. Thus the resulting map is $(\eta^d_{C_UF}\otimes a_B)\circ t^U_{F,rB}$. All equalities here are substitutions and naturality of the named maps; none uses that a projection map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison, expanded unit-mate calculation with Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback

proof.text:
Put $q=(1\otimes a_B)\circ t^U_{F,rB}:C_UN\to C_UF\otimes_A sC_XB$ and denote the right-hand side in the statement by $R$. The unit equation of [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization], now at $N$, and naturality of $\eta^d$ with $q$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
\Psi(R)&=s(\kappa^d)\circ sd(q)\circ s(c_N)\circ a_{eN}\circ C_U(\eta^e_N)\\
&=s(\kappa^d)\circ sd(q)\circ\eta^d_{C_UN}\\
&=s(\kappa^d)\circ\eta^d_{C_UF\otimes_A sC_XB}\circ q.
\end{aligned}$$
Under $d\dashv s$ the defining unit prescription for $\kappa^d$ says precisely
$$\rho^d_{dC_UF,C_XB}\circ s(\kappa^d)\circ\eta^d_{C_UF\otimes_A sC_XB}=\eta^d_{C_UF}\otimes1_{sC_XB}.$$
Consequently $\rho^d_{dC_UF,C_XB}\circ\Psi(R)=(\eta^d_{C_UF}\otimes a_B)\circ t^U_{F,rB}$, the same map obtained in step 3. The pro-etale open adjunction and its unit are those supplied in step 1, not a stalkwise substitute.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison: comparison by adjunction, with the pro-etale unit and tensor adjoint written explicitly

proof.text: Steps 3 and 4 give $\rho^d\Psi(L)=\rho^d\Psi(R)$. Cancel the isomorphism $\rho^d$; injectivity of the Hom bijection $\Psi$ from step 1 then gives $L=R$. This proves the displayed equality with exactly the source and target stated in the item.

source.place: Tag 09AF, lemma-jshriek-comparison: uniqueness through adjunction; final cancellation

proof.text: Finally let $f:F\to F'$ and $b:B\to B'$. The naturality square for the etale unit, tensored with $r(b)$, gives equality of the transposes of the two candidate naturality composites for $\kappa^e$, hence equality of the composites by the etale Hom bijection. The same argument with the pro-etale unit and $s(b)$ proves naturality of $\kappa^d$. The maps $a,c,t^T$ are natural by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], [lem-sf-open-comparison-unit-normalization], and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. Composition and tensoring of these commuting squares proves that $L$ and $R$ are natural in both $F$ and $B$, completing the naturality clause.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q65-d3668d4f6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, all six steps and every cited node statement, and re-derived each step: it is a correct agent-written proof with no new nodes and no fixes. The statement is unchanged and well typed; both sides go from C_X e(F⊗rB) to dC_UF⊗C_XB. Coefficients are ordinary constant-A modules with A finite, so no base-change morphism or other coefficient category is involved. Step 1: the unit normalization at N gives Ψ(h)=s(h c_N^{-1})η^d, and d⊣s comes from lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact once lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization identifies the site; def-weil-extension-by-zero defines d by exactly that presheaf. So Ψ is injective without faithfulness of s. Step 2: I checked the tensor square (*) from product naturality of a, the pure-tensor values in lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison (applied to the transported projections, with lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact clause 1), and the rule in def-weil-pbc-ringed-tensor-section-calculus that pure pairings determine linear maps. Marking it elementary is acceptable. Steps 3-4: both sides reduce to ρ^dΨ = (η^d_{C_UF}⊗a_B)t^U, using the transpose equations for κ^e and κ^d and the unit normalization at F and at N; the orientations are correct. Steps 5-6 (cancellation and naturality) are fine, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. Sources: Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison, l.5076) is only the adjoint argument, so proof_origin=agent is right; sites-modules Tag 03EL (l.3649) gives the bilinear-pairing route; the blueprint main-20261015 final pro-etale paragraph of lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula is the recorded place. Small cases checked: j=id, U empty, F=0, B=0, A=0. Duplicate search: lem-pur-open-projection-site-transport is a derived statement for locally free shifted F only, and lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization is pro-etale-only base change; neither is a duplicate. There is no cycle and no SGA. I accept the seven declared tool uses: lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction, lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization, lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor, lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact clause 1 only, lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison and lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback. lean.statement: theorem openComparison_tensor_normalization (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] {U X : Scheme.{u}} (j : U ⟶ X) [IsOpenImmersion j] : (∀ (F : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)) (B : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)), openComparisonTensorLeft A j F B = openComparisonTensorRight A j F B) ∧ (∀ {F F' : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)} {B B' : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A)} (f : F ⟶ F') (b : B ⟶ B'), (comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).map ((Etale.openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).map (f ⊗ₘ (Etale.openImmersionRestriction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).map b)) ≫ openComparisonTensorLeft A j F' B' = openComparisonTensorLeft A j F B ≫ ((openImmersionLowerShriek (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) j).map ((comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) U).map f) ⊗ₘ (comparisonUpperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) X).map b))
